newsitem.title: UK: Higher UK retail coffee prices seen by May - group.
newsitem.headline: Higher UK retail coffee prices seen by May - group.

text.p: The current sharp hike in arabica raw coffee prices could filter through the UK retail sector by May, an industry group said on Monday.
The Beverage Service Association (BSA), repsenting 85 UK coffee supply firms, said there had been a 70-percent jump in New York-traded arabica coffee futures prices since Christmas.
"This level of increase is bound to feed through... on-the-shelf prices by May," BSA chairman George Miller said in a statement.

He said major roasters in Germany, the Netherlands and the United States had already raised their prices and "it is inevitable that prices from British roasters will rise significantly in the very near future," he said.
He said prices of the higher-quality arabicas, grown mainly in central and south America, were continuing to rise and were forecast by experts to go higher.
He said better world demand for arabica beans coupled with supply shortages from some producer countries looked likely to drive prices higher.
Before this, Nestle UK and other major British roasters, their higher costs cushioned by the strength of sterling, have said that they had no immediate plans to boost retail values.
March coffee on the New York market closed on Friday at almost 178 U.S. cents a lb. This compared with 105 cents prior to Christmas.
Prices of the lower-quality robusta coffee, used mainly in instant coffee blend, have also risen by 43 percent since Christmas.
The rally in coffee is based on perception that stocks are low and that top grower Brazil may have a smaller crop, as well as labour problems in Colombia.
